- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.7) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots; cap forecast at 1–2% above recent peak.
- If sentiment turns negative (≤ 0.3) mid-horizon, model fails to adjust downward; apply downward bias of 1–2% per negative sentiment day.
- Model underestimates when sentiment is mixed or weak (0.0–0.3) — increase forecast by 0.5–1.5% to compensate for mean reversion bias.
- For 30-day forecasts, model often lags by 1–3 days; shift forecast up by 0.5–1.5% for each lagged day.
- If sentiment history shows strong positive sentiment followed by a drop, model tends to overcorrect; reduce forecast by 1–2% after sentiment drop.
